Hi Irene,

Thanks for the call this morning. After reviewing internally we have one additional commercial ask before we can move to legal redlines: we want a mechanism that goes beyond credits for repeated critical outages. Specifically: 

- If a 3rd-party operational audit (we'd nominate an auditor) confirms systemic failure to meet P1 uptime or median latency SLOs across two consecutive months, Medisys requires the ability to terminate for convenience with a 60-day notice and a capped fee (to cover our remediation and switching costs) held in escrow.
- We'd like the escrow amount to be staged (e.g., 1 month of committed spend initially, increasing to 3 months after the 2nd confirmed breach).

We are open to objective trigger language (audit scope, sample size, thresholds) and to an agreed neutral custodian for the escrow. Can your team draft a short term sheet or sample phrasing that we can circulate with our procurement/legal?

Regards,
Rajesh
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
Medisys Health

Hi Rajesh,

Appreciate the clarity — this is a reasonable request to capture in a term sheet so both sides have clear, objective triggers and a defined remedy path. We'll draft language that: 

1) Defines the audit scope and an agreed list of metrics (P1 uptime, median 99th latency, and availability of KV cache) and sample windows.
2) Specifies the auditor selection process (mutual nomination or neutral pool) and a single binding report to determine whether the "audit trigger" is met.
3) Describes escrow mechanics: initial capped amount = 1x monthly committed spend, increases to 3x after second confirmed audit within a rolling 12 months. Escrow custodian to be a neutral third party (e.g., escrow agent).
4) Allows a 60-day termination right for Medisys if audit confirms systemic failure; Redwood keeps the right to cure within a defined 30-day operational remediation window prior to escrow drawdown.

I'll loop in Aditya and Monica from legal and commercial for suggested drafting and a short term sheet by EOD tomorrow. Two quick Qs so we align: (a) is Medisys comfortable with a 30-day cure window once the auditor issues findings? (b) do you want the escrow drawn down automatically on termination, or only on a proven direct cost claim (e.g., switching/repurchase expense)?

Thanks,
Irene
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Aditya / Monica — forwarding Rajesh's note. Key commercial asks: third-party audit triggers termination right; staged escrow (1x -> 3x); 60-day termination window; 30-day cure; neutral custodian.

Suggested approach: 
- Propose an objective audit clause (see bullets below) and offer Redwood the right to commission a second, binding technical review if initial auditor deems failure (split cost). This reduces false positives.
- For escrow mechanics: offer automatic release on a corroborated, documented direct cost claim up to the escrow cap, plus portion release on termination to cover transition costs. Keep total liability capped (e.g., escrow = exclusive cash remedy beyond credits).
- Keep liquidated damages label out; call it "transition & remediation escrow" to avoid multiplying liability language.

Drafting ask: can you produce a 1-page term sheet that covers trigger language, selection process for auditor, cure timelines, escrow staging, and sample math for a $150k monthly committed spend? I want to have something to return to Rajesh tomorrow.

Thanks — Irene

Irene — thanks for the quick response and for proposing the cure window. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- We prefer the auditor's report to be final and binding for the trigger (to avoid long disputes). If Redwood wants a second review, Medisys would expect Redwood to pay that cost unless the second review materially contradicts the first.
- For the escrow release, we are open to an approach that splits the escrow: 50% automatically available to cover documented transition costs on termination; 50% reserved for claims proven against direct quantifiable losses.

If you can get the term sheet today it would help accelerate our legal review. We're hoping to keep the program on the table for a September go-live.

Best,
Rajesh

Subject: Term sheet (draft) — third-party audit trigger and escrow mechanics

Rajesh / team — attached is a short draft term sheet that captures the framework we discussed. High-level points: 

- Trigger: confirmed failure of P1 uptime or agreed latency SLOs across a rolling 30-day window, validated by a mutually agreed neutral auditor.
- Auditor process: each side nominates one firm from an agreed pool; the two nominees jointly appoint a neutral auditor. Initial audit cost split 50/50. Redwood may request a second binding technical review; if the second review disagrees with the first on material facts, Redwood will bear the cost; otherwise Redwood bears the cost only if discrepancies are immaterial.
- Cure & termination: Redwood has a 30-day cure period after the binding auditor report. If, after the cure period, the auditor confirms failure and remediation is insufficient, Medisys may provide 60 days' written notice to terminate for convenience.
- Escrow staging: escrow amount = 1x monthly committed spend upon execution; escalates to 3x after a second confirmed audit within a rolling 12-month period. Escrow custodian = neutral escrow agent. 
- Escrow release: on termination 50% of escrow is available for documented transition costs; the remaining 50% is reserved for proven direct costs (invoices/receipts) subject to a simple claims process. Total cash remedy (escrow) is exclusive and capped at the escrow amount.

Next steps: 
1) Aditya & Monica will convert this into a single-page term sheet and highlight any legal redlines.
2) Rajesh, please confirm you are comfortable with the auditor selection language and the 50/50 escrow split.
3) If agreed, we will circulate to our respective legal teams and attach the term sheet to the master SOW.

Thanks — aiming to close the commercial path today/tomorrow.

Irene
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
